Article.ArticleTitle: The ankyrin-like protein AnkB interacts with CatB, affects catalase activity, and enhances resistance of Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae and Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzicola to phenazine-1-carboxylic acid.

Abstract.AbstractText: Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae (Xoo), which causes rice bacterial leaf blight, and Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzicola (Xoc), which causes rice bacterial leaf streak, are important plant-pathogenic bacteria. A member of adaptor proteins family, ankyrin protein, was largely investigated in humans, but rarely in plant-pathogenic bacteria. In this study, a novel ankyrin-like protein, AnkB, was identified in Xoo and Xoc The expression of ankB was significantly up-regulated when these bacteria were treated with phenazine-1-carboxylic acid (PCA). ankB is located 58 bp downstream of the gene catB (which encodes a catalase) in both bacteria, and the gene expression of catB and catalase activity were reduced following ankB deletion in Xoo and Xoc Furthermore, we demonstrated that AnkB directly interacts with CatB by Gluthathione-S-transferase (GST) pull-down assays. Deletion of ankB increased Xoo and Xoc sensitivity to H2O2 and PCA, decreased bacterial biofilm formation, swimming ability and EPS production, and also reduced virulence on rice. Together our results indicate that the ankyrin-like protein AnkB has important and conserved roles in antioxidant systems and pathogenicity in Xoo and XocIMPORTANCE This study demonstrates that ankyrin protein AnkB directly interacted with catalase CatB in Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae and Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzicola Ankyrin protein AnkB can affect the gene expression of catB, catalase activity and sensitivity to H2O2 In Xanthomonas spp., the location of genes ankB and catB, and the amino acid sequence of AnkB are highly conserved. It's suggested that, in prokaryotes, AnkB plays a conserved role in the defense against oxidative stress.
